item.title: SCOTUS: Postal Service can’t be sued for ‘intentional’ failure to deliver mail
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled the FTCA’s postal exception bars claims over intentional mail nondelivery, shielding USPS under sovereign immunity.

item.title: With witnesses, trust is key
item.description: Lawyers have to develop a bond with a witness in order to develop trust. Because without trust, we’re flying blind.

item.title: Are disparate impact discrimination claims still viable?
item.description: Recent action by the U.S. Department of Justice has created uncertainty regarding the status of disparate impact discrimination cases.

item.title: Financial services firm settles discrimination claim
item.description: The plaintiff was a middle-aged white woman who worked for a financial services firm. She had gender discrimination claims under Chapter 151B for failure to receive an internal promotion and also claims under the Massachusetts Equal Pay Act because she was not paid commensurately with some of her male colleagues.

item.title: Nursing home resident beaten by walker-wielding roommate
item.description: The plaintiff’s decedent, a resident of a nursing facility, was violently assaulted and killed by his roommate while lying in bed.
